API
Off: nothing listens.
Command line, without a window: reactio render, convert, calc, nmr, check… (reactio --help; see Command line.txt).

Commands: list, scheme, properties, calc, nmr, inchi, addSmiles, addReaction, addText, addChart, addRadar, import, delete, clear, undo, redo, clean, export, table, setStyle, setRole, setAmount, prefixStyle, picture, set, image, selection, select, atoms, highlight, check, saved, markSaved, zoom, readOnly, smilesFromName, addName (common names everywhere, systematic names in the apps); in the Mac, Windows and Linux apps also name, and the same commands from scripts on this computer (local API, see the documentation). The documentation describes the format.

OpenChemLib 9.25.1 (openchemlib-js, the JavaScript build of Thomas Sander's OpenChemLib), included unchanged except for packaging as a plain script, is used for 3D shapes and rotation (a likely conformer from its torsion data, then relaxed with its MMFF94s+ force field, the MMFF94s variant of MMFF94: T. Chem. 1999, 20, 720), for stereochemistry in SMILES (reading @/@@, writing stereo SMILES) and for comparing structures; licensed BSD-3-Clause.
  • The journal drawing styles, the color themes Publication, Presentation, Pastel and Jmol, and the CDX property table are taken from ReShiki (© 2026 Ameyanagi and ReShiki contributors, MIT OR Apache-2.0, used under MIT; ReShiki takes the CDX table from the published CDX documentation of CambridgeSoft); the Jmol element colors come from Jmol.
  • The look of the 3D styles (Ball and stick, Tubes, Spheres: ball, bond and outline sizes, shading and depth fog) follows the presets of xyzrender (© 2026 Alister S. Goodfellow, MIT); only these values were taken, the drawing is this project's own code.
  • Journal style values (ACS, Nature, RSC, Angewandte, Synthesis / Synlett) follow the publishers' guidelines for authors.
  • More abbreviations (OTES, DMTr, Lev, 2-py, C6F13…) and reagent names (AIBN, t-BuOK, KOAc…): the Beilstein Chemical Lookup Collection (BChemLookup, Beilstein-Institut, CC0 1.0); Reactio Draw's own labels come first.
  • The color theme Color-blind safe uses the colors of Okabe and Ito (M. Okabe, K. Ito, Color Universal Design, 2002), recommended for figures by B. Wong, Nat. Methods 2011, 8, 441.
  • Paste name (desktop apps): names are read by OPSIN 2.9.0 (D. M. Lowe et al., J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 739), shipped unchanged as a separate program next to the app and run with the Java installed on the computer; licensed MIT (its bundled libraries keep their own licenses).
  • Name (desktop apps): names are made by openclatura (A. Mirza, K. M. Jablonka, R. Fedorov; rule-based, after the IUPAC 2013 recommendations), run unchanged in the computer's own Python with RDKit; licensed MIT. Each name is read back with OPSIN and compared with the drawing.
  • NMR prediction: contains information from nmrshiftdb2 (S. Kuhn, N. E. Schlörer, Magn. Reson. Chem. 2015, 53, 582), which is made available here under the nmrshiftdb2 Database License. The shift tables were made by Reactio Draw from measured spectra in the 2026-03-15 export; tables and method are published with the source code (data/nmr).
  • Atomic weights, monoisotopic masses and isotope abundances: standard IUPAC/NIST values.
  • InChI and InChIKey: made by the InChI library (InChI Trust / IUPAC; licensed MIT), compiled unchanged to WebAssembly and kept in the page; it runs here, nothing is sent anywhere. Build files: tools/inchi with the source code.

Click an element to draw with it: then click an atom on the sheet to change it, or click empty space to start a bond from that element.
Inserts into the text or label being edited. Otherwise the symbol is copied to the clipboard.

Symbols you add stay in the table (dashed), in this browser or app; right-click one to take it out. Export settings takes them along.

My abbreviations
Groups that Contract Labels turns back into labels

Draw the group, put an attachment point (*, in Symbols) on the atom where it attaches, select it, type the label and press Save selection. A label has one attachment point. A radical (•) works as the attachment point too. In SMILES, the attaching atoms are bracket atoms with missing hydrogens, as in [CH2]; without one the first atom attaches. Use a label by pointing at an atom and pressing Enter. Your labels are kept in this browser or app; Export labels and settings takes them along.

Interface

How fast Ctrl+wheel and the trackpad pinch zoom the sheet (6× by default).

Colours of the panels and buttons. As the system follows the light or dark mode of your computer; Match the paper turns the panels dark on a dark paper (night blue, dark grey, black, blueprint) and light on a light one. The sheet keeps its own paper colour in every theme.

Accent colour

Buttons, selection and highlights of the interface; the drawing keeps its own colours. A colour too light or too dark to read is adjusted for each theme.

On: Esc finishes a text or an atom label you are typing and keeps it, the same as Enter. Off: Esc throws the typing away.

Full shows every group of buttons; a click on a group's ⋮ folds it into one menu, and another click unfolds it. Compact keeps the File buttons and puts the rest into four menus in one row: Arrange, Structure, Style and Text.

Drawing

How an element with a group, typed on an atom that already has bonds, is drawn. Typing it with a dash (N-Me) always puts the group on a bond.

How the prefix letter of tBu, iPr, sBu, nBu, OtBu, CO2tBu is written. New labels you type follow it; Apply to selection changes the labels of the selected structures (the whole sheet when nothing is selected).

How far a curved (mechanism) arrow drawn from or to an atom or the middle of a bond stays off it. An atom with a label always keeps at least a small gap, so the head does not run into its letters. Arrows already drawn keep their ends.

What Clean Up and Clean Up 2D do with a methoxy group drawn out as O and a line. A crowded group that Clean Up has to write as a label follows this too (OCH3 when Leave as drawn).

What Clean Up and Clean Up 2D do with a methyl drawn as the bare end of a bond (toluene, the CH3 of an ethyl). Ethane and the methyl of a methoxy written as OMe or OCH3 are left alone.

Warnings

On by default: an atom over or short of its normal valence gets a red dashed ring. Turned off, the rings are gone from the sheet, but the Analysis tab and the API op check still report the errors. The rings never appear in copies or exports either way.

Off by default, because racemic and unspecified centres are often drawn that way on purpose. The other kinds are switched on and off below.

Warnings on the sheet

Untick a kind to stop marking it. The red text of a label that is not understood stays; only its dashed frame goes. Nothing here is ever drawn in copies or exports.

New documents

Style of new documents

Set the open document the way you like it — drawing style (ACS, RSC…), heteroatom colours on or off, colour theme, paper, font, grid — and press Use this document's style: every new document starts that way. Apply to this document gives the open one that look. Reset: new documents take the look of the document that is open.

Toolbar layout

Drag any toolbar button to move it; drag a group by its ⋮ grip (or, on the left, its heading) to move the whole group between the panels. Reset puts every button back.

Settings file

Hotkeys, button layout, your labels and templates in one file, to keep or to move to another computer.

Hotkeys

Every command and tool can have its own key.

Click a key, then press the new key (Shift allowed). Esc cancels, Backspace removes the key. Saved in this browser.

Fixed keys
Escdeselect, close menus Del ⌫delete the selection, or the atom, bond, arrow or text under the pointer ←↑→↓move the hotspot between atoms and bonds (Shift: atom to atom); with a selection, nudge it (Shift: larger steps) Alt + ←→rotate the selection 15° (Shift: 1°) Ctrl + →clone the selection across a new arrow Ctrl + Ccopy the selection (or the whole drawing) as CDXML: other chemistry editors paste it with the same layout, arrows and text Ctrl + Vpaste structures, CDXML or SMILES Ctrl + wheel, middle buttonzoom; move the view
Mouse
Ring tool + click a bondfuse a new ring onto that bond (annulation), on the less crowded side Template + click a bond or an atoma bond: fuse your template onto it (norbornene, a chair, any ring system); an atom: it becomes one of the template's ring atoms (spiro inside a chain or ring); only an atom with one free bond left, or a template without a ring, gets it by a new bond. With the template taken up, Tab picks which of its bonds or atoms is used; a key given to a template in the Hotkeys tab does the same over a bond or an atom Right-click an arrowarrow menu: head, line, curve, equilibrium (with the Arrow tool a single click opens it) Double-click a reaction arrowselects the whole reaction: structures, reagents, plus signs and conditions Drag arrow handleslengthen or shorten the arrow (a curved one along its circle or oval; Alt: freely); the middle handle bends it; the edges of the selection box stretch it into an oval Alt + drag an arrow endmove the end freely (without Alt it follows the circle or oval) Click a table celledit it on the sheet: Enter saves, Tab next compound, Esc cancels; Role opens the role menu, Limiting picks the limiting reagent Alt + click mass, volume or amountmark it as the measured quantity (red bold); a value you type is marked automatically − fewer rows / + all rowsunder the sheet table: hide or show the empty rows (not exported) Ctrl/Cmd + dragcopy the selection Shift + dragmove along one axis Alt + dragmove without smart guides; while drawing a bond, any length and angle Drag the round handlerotate the selection (Shift: 15° steps)

Reaction Stoichiometry

1 equiv = —
Conditions

Two grids: everything that goes into the flask on the left, products on the right. Structures left of the arrow or above it go into the first grid, structures right of it into the second; without an arrow everything is a reactant. Pick each column's role (reactant, catalyst, solvent) in its header. Catalysts take equivalents in mol%. Every number carries its own unit, chosen automatically; type a unit to override it (100 µL, 0.2 mmol, 50 mM). Whatever you type into Sample Mass, Volume or Moles becomes the measured quantity and turns red and bold; the dot in the cell switches it by hand. Mark the limiting reagent and its equivalents become 1. Amounts typed for the limiting reagent set the scale of the whole reaction; amounts typed for any other reactant or catalyst update its equivalents. Mass to weigh accounts for the reagent's weight %. For reagent solutions set the molarity and the volume follows from it; for neat liquids the volume follows from density, which fills in automatically for common solvents and liquid reagents. For solvents, Molarity is the concentration of the limiting reagent in that solvent; the total over all solvents is shown below the grids and can be typed in too. Products have their own rows: expected mass and moles, measured mass, purity, product mass and moles, and yield. The sheet starts with an example: aspirin synthesis.
